sources.title: The Medieval Economy of Assam
sources.note: Amalendu Guha on fragmented post-Kamrup politics, rice economy, early Ahom settlement, offices, domains, and service obligations.

sources.title: The history of mediaeval Assam, AD 1228 to 1603
sources.note: Nagendra Nath Acharyya doctoral thesis abstract and repository record covering sources, neighboring polities, early settlement, and gradual expansion.

sources.title: Moidams nomination dossier
sources.note: Official nomination history for Siu-ka-pha, family migration, the small initial realm, Charaideo, wet rice, shrines, and royal burial.

sources.title: Laying the Foundations
sources.note: Cambridge chapter on the Brahmaputra Valley setting and the early thirteenth-century Tai-Ahom arrival tradition.

sources.title: Annals of the Delhi Badshahate
sources.note: Digitized historical synthesis for the 1205-06 inscription, Ghiyasuddin campaign, Yuzbak invasion, floods, defeat, and death.

sources.title: The History of Medieval Assam
sources.note: Full monograph, especially the Kamrup or Kamata chapter, with explicit warnings that early royal dates are rough estimates.

sources.title: Protected Archaeological Sites and Monuments
sources.note: Government of Assam records for Kanai Borosibowa, Ambari, Charaideo, early medieval remains, and later evidence that must not be back-projected.

sources.title: Rock Art in Assam field report
sources.note: IGNCA multidisciplinary field report locating Kanai Barasi and documenting its 1206 inscription, other engravings, geology, damage, and multilayered history.

sources.title: Ambari Archaeological Site excavation
sources.note: Archaeological Survey of India description of Ambari occupation phases, hearths, floors, pottery, and tightly stated ceramic date ranges.

sources.title: Master Pieces of Assam State Museum
sources.note: Official museum catalogue identifying an Ambari Nataraja sculpture as thirteenth to fourteenth century.

sources.title: Moidams, the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
sources.note: UNESCO property account for Charaideo, long-lived royal funerary practice, mounds, water features, grave goods, and continuing rituals.

sources.title: Linguistic Features of the Ahom Bar Amra
sources.note: Cambridge linguistic account of Ahom as a Southwestern Tai language used in a multilingual kingdom and later court and ritual settings.

sources.title: Fixing chronology in Tai-Ahom chronicles using astronomical references
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Indian Institute of Astrophysics study showing why later chronicle dates require independent chronological testing.

sources.title: An Epigraphical Journey to an Eastern Islamic Land
sources.note: Mohammad Yusuf Siddiq study in Muqarnas, pages 83 to 108, providing scholarly epigraphic context for eastern inscriptions.

sources.title: Introduction to Assam
sources.note: Digitized regional history noting the epigraphic gap after the mid-twelfth century and printing the Kanai Barasi Sanskrit text.

sources.title: History of Northeast India, Theme 3
sources.note: Indira Gandhi National Open University teaching unit summarizing debated Prithu and Kamata origins and the obscure early royal sequence.

sources.title: District Census Handbook, Nagaon
sources.note: Official Census of India district history preserving a concise traditional sequence of Prithu, invasions, and Sandhya.

sources.title: Historical Monuments of Assam
sources.note: Government overview distinguishing Ambari seventh-to-twelfth and thirteenth-to-seventeenth-century layers and cataloguing its ceramics.

sources.title: Identification and Exploration of Archaeological Sites and Monuments
sources.note: Assam Directorate of Archaeology explanation of artifacts, fixed features, ecofacts, context, and the evidentiary limits of exploration.

sources.title: A History of Assam
sources.note: Sikkim University repository copy of Edward Gait’s 1926 synthesis, useful as an older compilation to compare with later critical work.

sources.title: The Origin of the Ahoms
sources.note: Royal Asiatic Society article identifying old Ahom buranji tradition as a source for migration narratives and mythical royal origins.

sources.title: Man and Environment, volume 1
sources.note: Archaeological report on kaolin pottery around Ambari and Marakdola, with a stated Ambari range ending in the twelfth century.

sources.title: Old Handicraft Industries in Assam
sources.note: Government of Assam overview of regional craft traditions, village-name evidence, pottery, and riverbed gold washing, used only with dating caution.
